newsitem.title: JAPAN: FOCUS - Worries mount in Japan over Russia PGM sales.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Worries mount in Japan over Russia PGM sales.

text.p: Japanese traders are worried about a possible change in Russia's sales strategy for platinum group metals after Russian central bank officials talked with a limited number of Japanese trade houses in Tokyo on PGM sales this week.
Bank officials met the trading houses to research Japan's precious metals market, with an eye toward the bank's future role as a seller of platinum group metals, the traders said.
The bank officials were told how much PGM the trade houses hope to buy from Russia, but no export contracts were signed.
Japanese traders said the visit implied the apparent shifting of power to the central bank from Almazjuvelireexport, the agency which has been handling Russia's PGM exports.
Almaz has been Russia's sole exporter of PGM and had long-term contracts with 13 Japanese companies, including seven trade houses and three bullion houses.

"I think the Russian central bank will certainly be able to sell PGM in the future. All bureaucratic agencies in Russia want to handle PGM since they need the foreign currency," said Yukuji Sonoda, president of Sumisho Gold Co Ltd.
"But it's uncertain at this stage what is going to happen with Almaz's export quota. The Japanese palladium market would be in confusion if there are two PGM suppliers," he said.
In Moscow, however, a senior Russian central bank official said on Tuesday that the bank did not intend to sell precious metals directly to Japanese customers.
In the precious metal market, the widely spread views are that the Almaz's export quota would be reduced sharply, and concerns are mounting about the stable metal supplies from Russia.

"The central bank lacks the know-how of long-term contracts. If the central bank will sell the metals, the sales would be through the spot market, not on long-term contracts," an official of a major bullion house said.
Traders said there will likely be more confusion, but they are divided over the near-term price direction for palladium.

"Palladium prices are expected to head lower. The central bank will start selling PGM in the spot market after the delegation is back in Russia. Russia will be forced to sell the metals as they desperately need money," one trader said.
Another trader said he was sceptical over a smooth power shift in Russia's jurisdiction over PGM.
"In a country where everything takes time, I'm doubtful about a smooth power shift taking place. The recent news indicates that Russia is in political chaos. Everything is uncertain," he said.
The trip has been shrouded in confusion. Late last week, a senior Russian central bank representative denied there was any such trip to Japan.
But First Deputy Prime Minister Antoly Chubais said the mission was going and Russian central bank officials were seen by Reuters in Tokyo, although they declined comment on their purpose.
Shipments of PGM from Russia to Japan have been halted since the beginning of the year, and the Japanese palladium market has become increasingly tight.
